label: early copy-phase outputs of very short sequences (L=3 outputs 2-3, L=4 output 2)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never on original tokens or the <DEL> step), and only for short sequences: L=3 (27% of steps active, 60% of mass) and L=4 (39% of mass); L>=5 is essentially silent. Within those it fires on the second and third outputs (recall_idx 1-2, i.e. the step right after <DEL> echoes orig(0) back as input, and the step after that). Strongest and most reliable at L=3, recall_idx=1 (predicate precision 1.0 there, holds the top activations, e.g. c b v <DEL> [c]); L=3 recall_idx=2 and L=4 recall_idx=1 fire about 40-60% of the time; L=4 recall_idx=2 is weaker (~15%). At L=4 the firing rate depends on the input token in a graded way (c, n, f, j high; p, m, d, z rarely), which the predicate does not capture, so precision is about 0.5. Does not fire on first-occurrence inputs, at recall_idx 0, or for long sequences. Dev: P 0.51, R 0.79, F1 0.62, mass recall 0.90.
